Everything below came from the new ONNX

No PyTorch anywhere: onnxruntime, the new export with its durations output, and the pure-Python tokenizer. This is the path that can ship in the app.

It is the same audio. Against the torch checkpoint on all 12 words at lengthScale 1.5: identical sample counts, worst max-abs difference 2.5e-06, correlation 1.00000000 on every word. So anything you hear here is the model, not the conversion.
even = final-phoneme duration ÷ median. 1.00 is even. The red rows are direct synthesis; the green rows are cut out of the carrier “Iri jambo ni <word>.” using the alignment the new export provides.
The blue row is fp16 — the 72 MB half-precision build, half the size of the 141.8 MB fp32 one, with float32 inputs and outputs so it is a drop-in swap. The number beside it is its waveform correlation against fp32 for that word (0.9989–0.99998, worst case inka).

The thing that had to be checked: cropping is frames × 256 = samples, so a frame count drifting by one in half precision would cut the word in the wrong place. It does not — the predicted durations come back as identical integers on all 12 words. fp16 is safe for this use.

If you cannot hear fp32 from fp16, ship fp16: it halves the asset.
